back: Houses of stone: the origin of the name Zimbabwe.
About 1220-1290 CE, on the Limpopo near the Shashe confluence.

front: What famous gold object was found at Mapungubwe?
back: A small golden rhinoceros, in a royal grave on the hilltop.

front: When was Great Zimbabwe at its height?
back: About the thirteenth to fifteenth centuries; it declined in the fifteenth century.

front: Name the three main parts of Great Zimbabwe.
back: Hill Complex, Great Enclosure (with the conical tower), Valley Ruins.
Building with shaped stone blocks fitted together without mortar.

front: Name four factors in the rise of Great Zimbabwe.
back: Cattle, agriculture, control of the gold and ivory trade with the coast, good location, religion and leadership.
Environmental exhaustion; shift of trade routes north; succession disputes; salt shortage; drought.

front: Who proved Great Zimbabwe was African-built?
back: David Randall-MacIver (1905) and Gertrude Caton-Thompson (1929); later radiocarbon dating confirmed it.
Payments in goods or labour by subjects or conquered chiefs to a ruler, showing loyalty.
